subject.title: Org owners cannot roll back latest after accidental higher-version skill publish

question: Should owner recovery use a narrow `delete --version … --replacement <version>` workflow that atomically repoints `latest`, or should ClawHub support a general owner tag-management command?
rationale: Both approaches change a public release-management surface, but the narrower replacement flow better limits accidental tag changes and makes rollback intent auditable.

options.title: Add explicit replacement rollback
options.body: Require a same-skill, available replacement version and atomically repoint `latest` while withdrawing the accidental version.

options.title: Add general owner tag management
options.body: Authorize organization publisher admins to manage arbitrary skill tags, including `latest`, with clear API and CLI documentation.

options.title: Keep staff-assisted recovery
options.body: Retain the current owner workflow and require moderator intervention for any latest-pointer correction.

recommendation.title: Add explicit replacement rollback
recommendation.body: Require a same-skill, available replacement version and atomically repoint `latest` while withdrawing the accidental version.

likelyOwner.reason: Current code identifies the publishing surface but not a reliable individual owner without repository-history access.
